enonce.texte:
Match the English telephone expressions with their French translations.

  • 1. Hello, may I speak to...?
  • 2. Hold on, please.
  • 3. Can I leave a message?
  • 4. I'll call you back.
  • 5. Wrong number.

Translations: A. Je vous rappelle. B. Mauvais numéro. C. Allô, puis-je parler à...? D. Ne quittez pas, s'il vous plaît. E. Puis-je laisser un message?

questions.texte: Match each English expression with its French translation.

enonce.texte: Complete the following telephone conversations with the correct polite expressions.

questions.texte: You call a company. The receptionist answers. You say: 'Hello, _______ I speak to the manager, please?'
The person you want is not available. You say: 'Can I _______ a message?'
You need to put the phone down for a moment. You say: '_______ on, please.'
You want to end the call politely. You say: 'Thank you for your time. _______'

enonce.texte:
You call your friend but they are not available. Their voicemail asks you to leave a message. Write a short message (3-4 sentences) including:

  • Your name
  • The reason for your call
  • A request for a callback

Use polite telephone expressions.

questions.reponse: Hello, this is Sarah. I'm calling to ask about our meeting tomorrow. Could you please call me back when you have a moment? My number is 654321. Thank you. Goodbye.

enonce.texte: You answer the phone at your office. The caller asks to speak to your colleague, but your colleague is busy. Write down the message you would take.

questions.texte: Write a complete phone message including the caller's name, the message, and a contact number.
questions.reponse: Message for: Mr. Jean Ndi. Caller: Mr. Pierre Kamga. Message: Please call back about the meeting on Friday. Phone number: 69876543. Time: 10:30 AM.

enonce.texte: Rewrite the following sentences using the imperative to give instructions on how to use a phone or make a call.

questions.texte: You must not talk too loudly.
You should listen to the instructions carefully.

enonce.texte:
Read the following scenario and write a complete dialogue. Then practice it with a partner.

Scenario: You are a receptionist at a hotel. A customer calls to book a room for two nights. The customer asks about the price and the availability.

questions.texte: Write a complete telephone dialogue between the receptionist and the customer.
questions.reponse: Receptionist: Good morning, Hotel Douala. How may I help you? Customer: Hello, I would like to book a room for two nights, please. Receptionist: Certainly. For which dates? Customer: From the 15th to the 17th of July. Receptionist: Let me check... Yes, we have availability. Customer: How much does it cost? Receptionist: It is 50.000 CFA per night. Customer: That's fine. I'll take it. Receptionist: Could I have your name, please? Customer: My name is Marie Nana. Receptionist: Thank you, Ms. Nana. Your reservation is confirmed. Goodbye. Customer: Thank you. Goodbye.

enonce.texte: You are teaching a friend how to use a new smartphone. Write 5 imperative sentences giving instructions.

questions.texte: Write 5 imperative sentences to explain how to use a smartphone.
questions.reponse: 1. Turn on the phone by pressing the power button. 2. Enter your password. 3. Open the app store. 4. Search for WhatsApp. 5. Install the app.

enonce.texte: Read the two dialogues below. Identify which is a professional call and which is a personal call. Justify your answer.

questions.texte:
Dialogue A: 'Hey, what's up? Can you come over later?'
Dialogue B: 'Good afternoon, this is Mr. Smith. I am calling to confirm my appointment for tomorrow.'
questions.reponse: Dialogue A is a personal call because it uses informal language like 'Hey' and 'what's up'. Dialogue B is a professional call because it uses formal language like 'Good afternoon' and gives professional information.

enonce.texte:
Write a complete telephone script for a professional conversation. Choose one of the following scenarios:

  • Calling to reschedule a doctor's appointment.
  • Calling a company to ask about a job application.
  • Calling a friend to invite them to a party.

Your script must include at least 8 exchanges and use polite telephone expressions, the imperative, and appropriate language for the context.

questions.texte: Write a complete telephone script for your chosen scenario.
questions.reponse: Receptionist: Good morning, Dr. Mbock's office. How can I help you? Patient: Hello, this is Marie. I have an appointment tomorrow at 10 AM, but I need to reschedule. Receptionist: I understand. Let me check the schedule. What day would you prefer? Patient: Do you have availability on Thursday? Receptionist: Yes, we have an opening at 2 PM. Would that work for you? Patient: Yes, 2 PM is perfect. Receptionist: Great. I have moved your appointment to Thursday at 2 PM. Patient: Thank you very much. I appreciate it. Receptionist: You're welcome. Is there anything else? Patient: No, that's all. Goodbye. Receptionist: Goodbye.
